items.exemplar:
A. France's entry into the war after Saratoga (1778) gave the Americans money, munitions, and — decisively — a navy that bottled up Cornwallis at Yorktown.

B. America's vast size worked against the British: with few cities and poor roads across a huge wilderness, British armies could win battles but never deliver a knockout blow.

C. Britain enjoyed the advantage of the world's most powerful navy, which blockaded American ports and moved troops freely along the coast.
parts: A. Briefly explain ONE reason for the American victory in the Revolutionary War.
B. Briefly explain a SECOND reason for the American victory.
C. Briefly explain ONE advantage the British held in the war.
items.stimulus: Historian Gordon Wood argues that Britain lost America largely because 'the British never found a way to translate battlefield victories into political control of a vast, hostile countryside.'
